extra.message: User-controlled input from self.get_argument('username') and self.get_argument('password') is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject SQL (e.g. username = admin'-- ) to bypass authentication or dump the Users table. Use parameterized queries instead.

User-controlled input from self.get_argument('server') is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to os.popen('ping -c 3 ' + server). An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' or '$(...)') to achieve arbitrary OS command execution. Use subprocess with an argument list and shell=False, and validate the input.

User-controlled input from self.get_argument('file') is concatenated into a file path ('read/' + file_name) and opened without sanitization. An attacker can supply '../../etc/passwd' to read arbitrary files on the server (path traversal / arbitrary file read).

The StaticHandler uses the user-controlled URL path segment ('static/' + path) directly in os.path.join and open() without normalization or restriction. A request like /static/../server.py or /static/../../etc/passwd allows reading arbitrary files outside the static directory (path traversal / arbitrary file read).

The 'q' query parameter is rendered into search.html via {% raw query %} and {% raw link %} (inside a <script> block), which disables Tornado's HTML autoescaping. Additionally the handler sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 (line 88). This results in reflected Cross-Site Scripting; an attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g. q=</script><script>alert(1)</script> or q='-alert(1)-').
The handler explicitly disables the browser XSS auditor by setting the 'X-XSS-Protection' header to '0', weakening defenses against the reflected XSS present on this endpoint.

UploadHandler.post() accepts an arbitrary uploaded file and writes its raw body to disk using the attacker-controlled file extension (os.path.splitext(original_fname)[1]) with no validation of file type, size, or content. There is no authentication on this endpoint. This allows unrestricted file upload and potential denial of service via large/many files.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: Sensitive functionality (file upload at /upload and file read at /read, as well as the command-execution /server.html endpoint) is exposed without any authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated remote user can upload files, read server files, and trigger command execution.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Hardcoded user credentials (including admin/admin) are embedded in source code and inserted into the database. Hardcoded/weak default credentials allow trivial authentication bypass and are exposed to anyone with source access.

Tornado application is configured with 'debug': True. Debug mode exposes detailed stack traces and internal information to clients on unhandled exceptions, leaking sensitive data and aiding attackers. It should be disabled in production.

User passwords are stored in plaintext in the Users table (no hashing) and compared directly in the login query. Cleartext storage of passwords exposes all user credentials if the database is compromised.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password
